link.title: scRNA QC - Short vs Long Read Sequencing

entry.content:
Project: Compare Sequencing Platforms in Terms of Immune Repertoire Analysis

Sequencing Platforms: Illumina NextSeq short read vs PacBio+Kinnex long read

Assumptions:

Matched sample pairs were analyzed using short-read and long-read single-cell sequencing workflows generated from the same 10x Genomics cDNA libraries (verify the fluorescence intensity and molarity distribution with Bioanalyser). Sequencing libraries passed standard quality control metrics (e.g., PacBio, Table2 [1]; Illumina, Table3 [2]) and that comparable analytical tools and workflows were applied for both datasets.

Evaluation of immune receptor recovery across cell types [3]

  • Compare immune cell-type detection between sequencing methods by assessing whether specific populations (e.g., γδ T-cells) are differentially recovered. (PacBio/Kinnex passes if it recovers the same major immune populations without systematic loss of rare cell populations.)

  • Assess full-length paired-chain recovery within detected B-cell (e.g., H/L chains) and T-cell populations (e.g., α/β chains) across clonotypes to evaluate immune receptor reconstruction. (PacBio/Kinnex passes if it achieves higher full-length paired-chain recovery across individual single-cell barcodes.)

Evaluation of platform-dependent differences in recombination profiles and clonal architecture [4]

  • Comparison of V(D)J gene usage and recombination patterns across both BCR and TCR chains, including IGHV vs IGHD, IGHV vs IGHJ, IGKV vs IGKJ, and TRAV vs TRAJ gene combinations. Clonal architecture can also be evaluated using diversity metrics (e.g., Shannon diversity) for each immunoglobulin and T cell receptor chain. (PacBio/Kinnex passes if it yields a denser V(D)J matrix with higher read-count abundance and fewer dropouts (e.g., visualization with heatmap), and if it yields overall higher diversity.)

  • Method-specific and shared recombination patterns can also be summarized. CDR3 structure comparisons can include complete CDR3 recovery rate, CDR3 length distribution and CDR3 motif structure analysis between sequencing methods.(PacBio/Kinnex passes if it shows high proportion of CDR3 recovery rate, unbiased CDR3 length distribution (need more detailed inspection for actual CDR3 length), comparable CDR3 motifs while also capturing hidden sequence variants.)

References:

[1] PacBio. (2023). Kinnex single-cell RNA kit for single-cell isoform sequencing [Application note]. [PacBio](https://www.pacb.com/wp-content/uploads/Application-note-Kinnex-single-cell-RNA-kit-for-single-cell-isoform-sequencing.pdf)

[2] ChromiumTM Single Cell 3’ v2 Libraries -Sequencing Performance on Illumina® NextSeq® 500 Flow Cells. (n.d.). Retrieved from https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/4p3SmrSj1mYMiyyOewQyAW/d98c236816b15cf247990f47a4ae3ac4/CG000085_Technical_Note_Sequencing_Metrics_for_NextSeq_500.pdf)

[3] A comparison of long-read single-cell transcriptomic approaches Scoones, A. L. A., Lan, Y., Utting, C., Pouncey, L., Lister, A., Kudasheva, S., Mehta, N., Irish, N., Swarbreck, D., Gharbi, K., Haerty, W., Cribbs, A. P., Wright, D. J., & Macaulay, I. C. (2025). A comparison of long-read single-cell transcriptomic approaches. [https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.07.03.662955](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.07.03.662955)

[4] Systematic evaluation of long- and short-read RNA-seq for human peripheral blood Iwabuchi, S., Nasti, A., Okada, H., Takeshita, Y., Sato, T.-A., Urabe, T., Takamura, T., Tamura, T., Tajima, A., Matsubara, K., & Kaneko, S. (2026). Systematic evaluation of long- and short-read RNA-seq for human peripheral blood. NAR Molecular Medicine, 3(1). [https://doi.org/10.1093/narmme/ugag006](https://doi.org/10.1093/narmme/ugag006)

entry.title: Pomodoro App
entry.content:
Aim: Build pomodoro app on Macbook menubar

Features: Adjustable and continuous 30, 45, 60 min study time - 5, 10, 25 min break time with notification sound.

Requirements: Install SwiftBar app

brew install swiftbar

mkdir -p ~/SwiftBarPlugins

Create python script:

nano ~/SwiftBarPlugins/pomodoro.1s.py

Paste this Python Code into pomodoro.1s.py:

Change the path to your Python location using: which python3

```python #!/path.../bin/python3 #Change Me import json import os import subprocess import sys import time state_file_path = os.path.expanduser("~/.pomodoro_state.json") default_timer_state = { "running": False, "mode": "Focus", "focus_minutes": 30, "break_minutes": 5, "end_time": 0 } def load_timer_state(): if not os.path.exists(state_file_path): return default_timer_state.copy() try: with open(state_file_path, "r") as state_file: saved_timer_state = json.load(state_file) return {**default_timer_state, **saved_timer_state} except Exception: return default_timer_state.copy() def save_timer_state(timer_state): with open(state_file_path, "w") as state_file: json.dump(timer_state, state_file) def send_notification(notification_title, notification_message): subprocess.run([ "osascript", "-e", f'display notification "{notification_message}" with title "{notification_title}"' ]) subprocess.run([ "afplay", "/System/Library/Sounds/Glass.aiff" ]) def start_timer(): timer_state = load_timer_state() selected_minutes = timer_state["focus_minutes"] if timer_state["mode"] == "Focus" else timer_state["break_minutes"] timer_state["running"] = True timer_state["end_time"] = int(time.time()) + selected_minutes * 60 save_timer_state(timer_state) def stop_timer(): timer_state = load_timer_state() timer_state["running"] = False timer_state["mode"] = "Focus" timer_state["end_time"] = 0 save_timer_state(timer_state) def set_focus_minutes(minutes_value): timer_state = load_timer_state() timer_state["focus_minutes"] = minutes_value if not timer_state["running"] and timer_state["mode"] == "Focus": timer_state["end_time"] = 0 save_timer_state(timer_state) def set_break_minutes(minutes_value): timer_state = load_timer_state() timer_state["break_minutes"] = minutes_value if not timer_state["running"] and timer_state["mode"] == "Break": timer_state["end_time"] = 0 save_timer_state(timer_state) def switch_session_if_finished(timer_state): if timer_state["running"] and int(time.time()) >= timer_state["end_time"]: if timer_state["mode"] == "Focus": timer_state["mode"] = "Break" timer_state["end_time"] = int(time.time()) + timer_state["break_minutes"] * 60 send_notification("Pomodoro", "Focus finished. Take a break.") else: timer_state["mode"] = "Focus" timer_state["end_time"] = int(time.time()) + timer_state["focus_minutes"] * 60 send_notification("Pomodoro", "Break finished. Start focusing.") save_timer_state(timer_state) return timer_state def format_remaining_time(seconds_remaining): bounded_seconds = max(0, seconds_remaining) minutes_display = bounded_seconds // 60 seconds_display = bounded_seconds % 60 return f"{minutes_display:02}:{seconds_display:02}" def print_menu(): timer_state = switch_session_if_finished(load_timer_state()) if timer_state["running"]: remaining_seconds = timer_state["end_time"] - int(time.time()) print(f"{timer_state['mode']} {format_remaining_time(remaining_seconds)}") else: print(f"Pomodoro {timer_state['focus_minutes']}:00") print("---") if timer_state["running"]: print(f"Stop | bash='{sys.executable}' param1='{__file__}' param2='stop' terminal=false refresh=true") else: print(f"Start | bash='{sys.executable}' param1='{__file__}' param2='start' terminal=false refresh=true") print("---") print("Focus duration") for focus_option in [30, 45, 60]: selected_marker = "✓ " if timer_state["focus_minutes"] == focus_option else "" print(f"{selected_marker}{focus_option} min | bash='{sys.executable}' param1='{__file__}' param2='focus' param3='{focus_option}' terminal=false refresh=true") print("---") print("Break duration") for break_option in [5, 10, 25]: selected_marker = "✓ " if timer_state["break_minutes"] == break_option else "" print(f"{selected_marker}{break_option} min | bash='{sys.executable}' param1='{__file__}' param2='break' param3='{break_option}' terminal=false refresh=true") print("---") print("Reset | bash='{sys.executable}' param1='{__file__}' param2='stop' terminal=false refresh=true") if len(sys.argv) > 1: command_name = sys.argv[1] if command_name == "start": start_timer() elif command_name == "stop": stop_timer() elif command_name == "focus": set_focus_minutes(int(sys.argv[2])) elif command_name == "break": set_break_minutes(int(sys.argv[2])) sys.exit(0) print_menu() ```

Then run this code on Bash:

chmod +x ~/SwiftBarPlugins/pomodoro.1s.py

Finally, open the SwiftBar app. You will see SwiftBar appear in your MacBook menu bar. Click “Refresh All,” and the label will change to “Pomodoro {Time}”.
entry.summary: Aim: Build pomodoro app on Macbook menubar
